To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the cross sections of neutrino–deuteron reactions at energies relevant to the interpretation of the SNO experiment are 0.2±0.002 (0.1±0.002)×10−41 cm2 for neutrino (antineutrino) scattering, and 2.2±0 (2.2±1.2)×10−42 cm2 for neutrinos and antineutrinos combined.
the νd cross section for the reaction νd → p + n + e− is 2.3 ± 0.2 × 10−42 cm2 and that for the reaction νe + d → n + e+ + e− is (2.2 ± 0.1) × 10−41 cm2.
the νd cross section at 0.5 MeV is (1.5±0.1)10-42 cm2, that the νd reaction is a factor of ∼2.4 stronger than the νe p reaction, and that the νe p cross section is ∼0.8×10-42 cm 2.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the calculation of cross sections of the νd and νp processes at energies of the order of the solar-neutrino energies.
the calculation of the weak axial vector coupling of the deuteron to a neutrino.

the following aspects: (1) the calculation of the nuclear matrix elements of the neutrino–deuteron reactions at low energies, which is a crucial ingredient of the calculation of the neutrino-nucleus reactions; (2) the evaluation of the radiative corrections to the neutrino-deuteron cross sections, which are needed for the interpretation of the SNO experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, at the 1% level, the νd cross section is consistent with the results of the effective-field-theory calculation and with the results of our group.
the SNO experiment, in its present form and in combination with the other solar neutrino experiments, has provided a strong indication for the presence of neutrino oscillations.
the solar neutrino problem is solved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our new cross section estimates are in good agreement with those of other groups.
the neutrino-deuteron reaction cross sections are known to an accuracy of ∼10% for the energy region relevant for the solar neutrino problem.
the SNO experiment is now in good shape for extracting the neutrino oscillation parameters from the data.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for the solar neutrinos, the νd cross section is about 1.3 times larger than the νd cross-section value used in the SNO analysis.
the SNO experiment is sensitive to the 7Be neutrino flux at a level of 2–4%, which is comparable with the sensitivity of Borexino.
the SNO data, when combined with the νd reaction rate, can be used to extract the solar ν fluxes with 3% accuracy.
